desc:
The array preorder is the preorder traversal (node, then left subtree, then right subtree) of a binary search tree with distinct values. Rebuild the tree and return it in level-order encoding.

For a binary search tree, the preorder sequence determines the tree uniquely. Aim for O(n) time.

Tree encoding. A binary tree is written as an integer array in level order. The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn, level by level, from left to right. A missing child is written as -1 (real node values are never negative, so -1 cannot be confused with a value). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped. The empty tree is [].

For example, [5,2,7,-1,3,6] is the tree whose root 5 has left child 2 and right child 7; node 2 has no left child and right child 3; node 7 has left child 6 and no right child.

Example 1

preorder = [8,5,1,7,10,12]
Output: [8,5,10,1,7,-1,12]
Root 8; 5 and 10 are its children; 1 and 7 hang below 5; 12 hangs below 10 on the right.

Example 2

preorder = [1,2,3]
Output: [1,-1,2,-1,3]
constraints: preorder is the preorder traversal of some valid BST
hints: The first element is the root. Everything after it that is smaller belongs to the left subtree, and what follows belongs to the right subtree. Doing this naively can cost O(n²).
Instead of searching for the split point, think of inserting the values one by one into a BST in the given order: that reproduces exactly the original tree.

To avoid a full descent for every value, keep a stack of the nodes whose right child is still undecided. For each new value, pop every node smaller than it; the last popped node gets the value as its right child, otherwise the node on top of the stack gets it as its left child. Push the new value.
editorial: Inserting the values in preorder into an empty BST gives the original tree, because each node appears before all of its descendants. That is correct but may take O(n²) if the tree is a long chain.

The monotonic-stack version is linear. The stack holds the current left spine: values decrease from bottom to top. When a new value v arrives, every stack node smaller than v has finished its left subtree, so pop them; the last popped node is the deepest ancestor for which v belongs in the right subtree, so v becomes its right child. If nothing was popped, v is smaller than the top and becomes its left child. Each value is pushed and popped at most once: O(n). The final level-order output is one more O(n) pass.
